text:
Yara: Heads-up: saw a runtime error from a customer on Vercel Edge: "TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor" when importing the SDK in middleware. They used `import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-js-sdk'`.
Ibrahim: That smells like ESM default vs named export mismatch. Our package historically published a CJS default export and an ESM named export. Bundlers sometimes rewrite `import X from 'pkg'` into `require('pkg').default` which breaks in edge contexts.
Celeste: repro snippet: ```ts
// middleware.ts
import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-js-sdk'
export async function middleware(req: Request) {
  const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
  await c.generate({ prompt: 'ping' })
  return new Response('ok')
}
``` customers using Next + SWC + edge ran into the crash.
Ibrahim: two fixes: 1) stabilize exports so `import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-js-sdk'` behaves consistently in ESM build pipelines; 2) document and recommend named import: `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-js-sdk/edge'` for ESM edge users.
Yara: For (1) package.json should provide: `"main": "./dist/node.cjs", "module": "./dist/edge.mjs", "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/edge.mjs", "require": "./dist/node.cjs" }, "./edge": "./dist/edge.mjs" }` so ESM-aware bundlers get the ESM build.
Celeste: Also add `export default` in the ESM build to make `import X from 'pkg'` work: in rollup/ts build ensure `export default RedwoodClient` in edge.mjs while keeping named exports. But prefer encouraging `import { RedwoodClient }` to avoid ambiguity.
Ibrahim: Another wrinkle: SWC sometimes rewrites `export default` to `module.exports.default =` when packaging, causing consumers who expect a function constructor to get an object. Solution: add an explicit named subpath `./dist/edge.mjs` and a short compat shim `dist/edge-shim.js` that does `import mod from './edge.mjs'; export default mod.RedwoodClient ?? mod.default ?? mod; export * from './edge.mjs'` so both forms work.
Yara: We should also update types so `import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-js-sdk'` is typed. Add `export default RedwoodClient` in index.d.ts and in edge.d.ts to reduce TS surprises.
Celeste: Docs/README: update starter to use `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-js-sdk/edge'` and add a note: "Prefer named import in middleware; if you use default import, upgrade to 0.9.0+ which includes ESM compat shim."
Buildy: CI: added a small matrix job that builds a Next middleware fixture using SWC and esbuild to validate both import forms.
Ibrahim: Also add a migration lint rule in Starter repo that flags default imports from packages where we saw issues. Helps customers catch it early.
Docs-bot: drafting docs PR with examples for both correct imports + a troubleshooting section: "TypeError: X is not a constructor" -> check import form and upgrade to canary with ESM shim.
Yara: Nice. I'll open a tiny patch to generate an edge-shim and update package.json exports and types. Will ping for reviews.
